assets: historical audit trail keyed by canonical IDs
actors: publisher (proposes a label that is not the owner's)
attacker (supplies confusable/bidi/injection labels, stale caches, forged bindings)
operator (reviews display contract, never a study participant)
trust_boundaries: owner namespace -> canonical directory (petnames never cross without re-binding)
untrusted label input -> display envelope (validated, never authority)
display envelope -> approval gateway (canonical tuple only)
current projection -> historical audit (append-only, rename never rewrites)
visual UI -> accessibility tree (canonical ID in both)
hard_invariants: I1: canonical principal ID and scope are the sole authority identity
I2: petname is an owner-local, versioned, display-only projection
I3: reverse lookup petname->principal never authorizes an action
I4: collision returns explicit ambiguity, never auto-selects a principal
I5: approval binding holds canonical actor/target/operation/tool/version/canonical-args/expiry; petname is not in the authoritative tuple
I6: audit/history stores canonical IDs; rename/delete changes only the current projection, never past events
I7: untrusted labels never expand capabilities, policy, knowledge or scope
I8: canonical identity is available visually and non-visually in every high-impact view, approval and on-behalf banner

threats.description: identical petname assigned to two different principals in one owner namespace or across owners
threats.control: normalized (NFC+casefold) collision index; ambiguous envelopes list all matching canonical identities and require explicit canonical selection

threats.description: petname collision across scopes/owners/tenants treated as one identity
threats.control: scope-qualified keys (owner, tenant/scope, normalized petname); cross-scope reuse is a mismatch FAIL

threats.description: Unicode confusable, mixed-script, bidi control, invisible characters, normalization/case/whitespace collision silently accepted
threats.control: NFC+casefold comparison, confusable/mixed-script/bidi-invisible detectors; flagged or ambiguous, canonical ID always shown

threats.description: rename/delete/reuse and stale cache rebind a label to the wrong principal
threats.control: versioned projections with supersedes chain + tombstones; stale versions never re-resolve; history stays canonical

threats.description: forged on-behalf banner or approval display substitutes a friendly label for the canonical actor/target
threats.control: approval and on-behalf views render canonical actor/beneficiary IDs + scope + action; petname is annotation only

threats.description: name-only reverse lookup or auto-selection of the first match drives authorization
threats.control: search returns a candidate set; authorization requires an explicit canonical target; first-match selection is a FAIL

threats.description: XSS/HTML/script injection through an untrusted petname executes in the UI
threats.control: safe text API (textContent) only; CSP blocks inline/network execution; injection payloads render inert

threats.description: canonical ID lost in screen-reader/keyboard representation
threats.control: accessibility_text always carries canonical ID/type/scope; keyboard flow + visible focus; copy-ID control

threats.description: historical audit rewritten after rename (old events show the new label as identity)
threats.control: audit stores canonical IDs only; rename/delete emits a new projection version; past envelopes immutable

threats.description: external tool/document proposes an alias and attempts to widen authority
threats.control: external labels are untrusted data; publisher-vs-owner mismatch is flagged; scope mismatch FAILs

controls_summary: single authoritative display-envelope schema shared by UI, fixtures, importer and evaluator
fail-closed validation: unknown version/enum/field, duplicate JSON keys, NaN/Infinity, remote $ref, traversal, wrong type
no petname serialization in any field a consumer could mistake for a canonical ID
deterministic 40-case corpus with separate oracle; UI never sees the oracle
residual_risks: synthetic technical observations only (human_study_n=0); recognition improvement NOT_MEASURED
single-operator design review is not a population study
confusable detection is heuristic; novel scripts may need corpus extension
same-host replay is called replay, not an external audit
